title: target/ grows without bound under feature-powerset and mutation runs
description:
## What happened

The disk hit 100% (468K free of 907G) mid-session and the mutation sweep of pkix-revocation died with 'No space left on device'. target/ was 280G, of which target/debug was 278G.

## Measurements, 2026-11-27

* target/debug/build          226G
* target/debug/incremental     51G
* 2572 hash directories under target/debug/build/pkix-chain alone, 315 crate directories in total
* each hash dir holds one test binary in out/, e.g. aia_http_e2e-<hash> at 149 MB
* ONE clean full build of the workspace: 12G

So 278G was roughly 23 full builds' worth of artifacts, kept because cargo never garbage-collects the per-configuration hash directories.

## Why this workspace hits it harder than most

Three habits each multiply the configuration count:

* cargo hack --feature-powerset --depth 2 across 34 crates
* the per-feature doc job and the default-features job, which are separate configurations again
* cargo-mutants, which copies the tree per job and builds each copy -- 10 jobs is 10 more target dirs

Test binaries at 149 MB are the per-unit cost, and there are hundreds of them.

## Done

rm -rf target/debug freed 278G in 9 seconds. Full rebuild afterwards: 218 test suites, 0 failures, target back to 12G. Nothing else was touched -- target/release, the three no-std cross targets and target/doc were left alone.

## Options, none taken yet

1. An operational rule: clean before a mutation sweep or a powerset run, not after. Cheapest, and the sweep is the thing most likely to exhaust the disk.
2. A dev/test profile with debug = 'line-tables-only' or strip = 'debuginfo'. Most of a 149 MB test binary is debuginfo, so this could be a large win -- UNMEASURED, and it trades away debugging detail, which is a maintainer's call rather than mine.
3. cargo-mutants with fewer jobs. Each job is a tree copy plus its own build; 10 was what exhausted the disk.

Worth noting option 2 needs a measurement before anyone commits to it, and that this is build hygiene rather than a defect in any crate.
close_reason:
All three options are taken; the 'none taken yet' section was stale.

1. Operational rule: AGENTS.md line 374 says to run scripts/prune-build-exhaust.sh after a powerset or mutation run, and the 'Sweeps are I/O bound' section says to keep -j at 4 or below and not to run heavy workspace builds beside one.

2. The profile: [profile.dev] debug = 'line-tables-only' is set, with the measurement the bead asked for recorded beside it in Cargo.toml -- pkix-chain's aia_http_e2e test binary went from 135,767,128 to 52,864,152 bytes, 2.6x. The comment says what it gives up (variable inspection under a debugger) and how to get it back locally, which was the maintainer's call the bead flagged.

3. Fewer jobs: today's nine sweeps all ran at -j 3 or -j 2 without exhausting anything.

Verified now: target/debug is 20G against the 278G that filled the disk, and /data has 322G free after nine crate sweeps in one session, several of them re-run two or three times. The accumulation half -- Cargo keying artifacts by configuration hash and never collecting them -- is what the prune script handles, and it is the half that actually filled the disk.
